Baked mac and cheese is one of those dishes that can go from great to gluey and greasy over a 3-day hold, but only in a couple of specific spots — the pasta keeps drinking the sauce in the fridge, and the cheese sauce and any breadcrumb topping don't reheat well straight through. Here's how to build it Sunday so Wednesday tastes fresh, not reheated:

**Sunday — build it, but stop just short of "done":**
1. Cook the pasta noticeably less than al dente — pull it while it still has real bite (a minute or two short of the package time). It'll keep absorbing liquid all week, and full-cooked noodles turn to paste by Wednesday.
2. Make your cheese sauce (bechamel + cheese) a bit looser/thinner than you normally would — extra half cup or so of milk. The pasta will soak some of that up over the next three days, and a thin sauce now becomes the right consistency later instead of a dry casserole.
3. Mix pasta and sauce, put it in the baking dish, but **hold back the breadcrumb topping and about a half cup of extra shredded cheese** — bag them separately in the fridge. Bread crumbs that sit wet on top of a casserole for 3 days turn soggy and pasty, not crisp.
4. Bake it covered just until it's hot through and set (no need to brown or crisp anything, since you're not eating it yet) — roughly 20–25 minutes at 350°F. Cool, then cover and refrigerate.

**Wednesday — reheat and refresh:**
1. Pull it out and let it sit at room temp 20–30 minutes while the oven heats to 350°F.
2. Stir in a splash of milk (2–3 tbsp) right into the dish before it goes in — this rehydrates the sauce so it comes out creamy instead of dry-and-tight from the fridge.
3. Cover with foil, bake ~20 minutes until hot in the center.
4. Uncover, scatter the reserved raw breadcrumbs and cheese on top, and bake uncovered another 8–10 minutes, or run it under the broiler for the last minute or two, until the top is bubbling and golden. That's what gives you a fresh-baked crust instead of a soft, twice-baked one.

Here's a real 30-minute version — the trick is starting the rice immediately since it's your bottleneck, then building the chicken and sauce around it.

**Fast Lemon Chicken & Rice** (serves 4)

**Ingredients**
- 1 cup basmati or jasmine rice, rinsed
- 1½ cups chicken broth (or water)
- 1¼ lb chicken breast, sliced horizontally into thin cutlets (or thin-pounded)
- Salt and pepper
- 3 tbsp flour, for dredging
- 3 tbsp olive oil, divided
- 3 tbsp butter, divided
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest of 1 lemon + juice of 1½ lemons
- 1 cup chicken broth (for the sauce)
- Handful fresh parsley, chopped

**Method**
1. Put rice and 1½ cups broth in a small pot, salt lightly, bring to a boil, then cover and drop to low — 15 minutes, off heat. Do not lift the lid; let it sit covered once the timer's up so it stays fluffy while you finish the chicken.
2. While the rice cooks: season the cutlets with salt and pepper, dredge lightly in flour, shaking off excess.
3. Heat 2 tbsp oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high. Sear the cutlets 3-4 minutes a side, until deep golden and firm to the touch. Work in batches so they don't crowd — pull them to a plate once done.
4. Drop heat to medium, add remaining 1 tbsp oil, garlic, and lemon zest — 30 seconds, just until fragrant, don't let the garlic brown.
5. Pour in the 1 cup broth, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom. Let it bubble and reduce by about a third, 3-4 minutes.
6. Off the heat, stir in the remaining 2 tbsp butter and the lemon juice — adding the juice off heat keeps it bright instead of flattening into something bitter and dull. Taste and adjust salt.
7. Return the chicken to the pan to warm through in the sauce, 1 minute. Stir the parsley in at the very end so it stays fresh and green instead of wilting into the sauce.
8. Fluff the rice with a fork and serve the chicken and sauce spooned over it.

That's the whole 30 minutes if you start the rice the second you turn the stove on. Want me to save this one to the cookbook?
